negative_reviews.author: Ken Adams
negative_reviews.text: Waited entirely too long for food. 6 tables (4 seated before us) and we waited nearly an hour for food.

negative_reviews.author: CY
negative_reviews.text:
I recently visited Maki & Nori in Central London with my parents, and unfortunately the experience did not justify the price.

The service was disappointing from the start. Despite the restaurant being nearly empty, empty plates were rarely cleared from our table. We eventually had to stack them ourselves to make room, yet staff would often remove only one plate and leave the rest behind.

The restaurant’s signature hand roll trolley is an interesting concept, but the experience felt rushed rather than enjoyable. I ordered 2 of the A5 Wagyu hand roll (£15 each), and the server accidentally dropped part of the wagyu during each preparation without apologising or replacing it. After every bite, we were repeatedly asked for feedback and comparisons before we had even finished eating, which made it difficult to simply enjoy the food.

The tuna hand roll was decent, but overall the food was average. The wagyu in both the hand roll and nigiri was surprisingly chewy, and portion sizes were noticeably smaller than most sushi restaurants in London. I was also concerned to see containers of raw tuna sitting open on the hand roll trolley.

We spent £288 for three people. For the price, the food quality, portion sizes and service simply did not deliver.

If you’re looking for authentic, high-quality Japanese food, I don’t think Maki & Nori is worth the cost. The restaurant focuses heavily on the hand roll experience, but the food itself and overall dining experience fell well below expectations.
